QuestionText: HTML stands for
Explanation: HTML is the standard language for creating web pages.

QuestionText: A web browser displays web pages and is used to navigate the internet
Explanation: Browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) interpret HTML/CSS/JS to display web pages.

QuestionText: <!DOCTYPE html> declaration must be the first line of an HTML document
Explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> declares HTML5 document type to the browser.

QuestionText: The <body> tag contains all visible page content
Explanation: Everything visible on the page goes inside <body>.

QuestionText: The <head> tag contains metadata, title, and CSS links
Explanation: <head> contains non-visible page information: title, meta tags, CSS links.

QuestionText: The largest heading in HTML is <h1>
Options: D) All headings are same size
Explanation: <h1> is the most important/largest heading; <h6> is the smallest.

QuestionText: The <a> tag with href attribute creates a hyperlink
Explanation: Link text creates a clickable hyperlink.

QuestionText: The href attribute specifies the destination URL of a link
Explanation: href (hypertext reference) = the URL the link points to.

QuestionText: The tag uses src attribute to specify the image file
Explanation: displays an image.

QuestionText: The alt attribute in provides text for screen readers and when image fails
Explanation: alt text is essential for accessibility and fallback display.

QuestionText: <ul> creates an unordered (bullet) list and <ol> creates a numbered list
Explanation: <ul> = unordered (bullets), <ol> = ordered (numbers), both use <li> for items.

QuestionText: The <b> or <strong> tag makes text bold
Explanation: <b> and <strong> both render text bold; <strong> also conveys semantic importance.

QuestionText: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets
Explanation: CSS is used to style web pages (colours, fonts, layout, spacing).

QuestionText: CSS can be applied inline, internally, or via an external file
Explanation: Three CSS methods: inline style attribute, <style> in <head>, linked external .css file.

QuestionText: The CSS 'color' property sets text colour
Explanation: color: red; sets text to red. background-color sets the background.

QuestionText: HTML table uses <table>, <tr>, <th>, <td> tags
Explanation: <tr> = row, <th> = header cell, <td> = data cell.

QuestionText: The <form> tag collects user input on a web page
Explanation: <form> wraps input elements to collect and submit user data.

QuestionText: target='_blank' in an <a> tag opens the link in a new tab
Explanation: target='_blank' opens linked page in new browser tab/window.

QuestionText: HTTP is the protocol for transferring web pages between browser and server
Explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) defines browser-server communication for the web.

QuestionText: HTTPS adds encryption (SSL/TLS) to HTTP for secure communication
Options: C) HTTPS is only for emails
D) HTTPS is identical to HTTP
Explanation: HTTPS encrypts data in transit, protecting passwords and personal information.

QuestionText: The CSS class selector uses a dot (.) and the ID selector uses a hash (#)
Options: C) Class uses # and ID uses .
D) Both use the same symbol
Explanation: CSS: .className for class, #idName for ID. Classes reusable; IDs unique per page.

QuestionText: JavaScript adds interactivity and dynamic behaviour to web pages
Explanation: JavaScript enables dynamic content, form validation, animations, and user interaction.

QuestionText: A search engine indexes the web to return results for keyword queries
Options: C) A search engine hosts files
D) A search engine builds websites
Explanation: Search engines (Google, Bing) crawl, index, and rank web pages for user queries.

QuestionText: Responsive web design makes pages adapt to different screen sizes
Options: C) Makes pages load faster only
Explanation: Responsive design uses fluid grids and media queries to optimise layout for any screen.

QuestionText: CSS media queries apply styles based on screen/device properties
Explanation: @media (max-width: 768px) { } applies styles only when screen width is 768px or less.

QuestionText: The <canvas> element in HTML5 is used for drawing graphics with JavaScript
Explanation: <canvas> provides a JavaScript-controlled drawing surface for 2D graphics.

QuestionText: HTML5 semantic elements (<header>, <nav>, <article>) give meaning to page structure
Explanation: Semantic HTML5 elements improve readability, SEO, and accessibility by describing content meaning.

QuestionText: GET method sends data in the URL; POST sends data in the request body
Explanation: GET: data visible in URL (suitable for searching). POST: data hidden in body (suitable for forms, login).

QuestionText: CSS Flexbox creates flexible one-dimensional (row or column) layouts
Explanation: Flexbox: CSS layout model for distributing and aligning items along a single axis.

QuestionText: Web accessibility ensures websites are usable by people with disabilities
Explanation: Web accessibility (WCAG) ensures people with visual, auditory, or cognitive disabilities can use websites.

QuestionText: Cookies store small data files in the browser to remember user sessions
Explanation: Cookies: small text files stored by websites on the browser to persist session data, preferences, and login state.

QuestionText: DNS translates domain names like google.com into IP addresses
Explanation: DNS (Domain Name System): the internet's directory that converts human-readable domain names to IP addresses.

QuestionText: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network
Explanation: IPv4 address (e.g. 192.168.1.1) uniquely identifies each device on a network.

QuestionText: The <title> tag sets the text shown in the browser tab
Explanation: <title> in <head> sets the browser tab/window title and appears in search engine results.

QuestionText: An HTML attribute provides additional information about an HTML element
Explanation: Attributes appear inside the opening tag and modify element behaviour: , .

QuestionText: The <ul> list items have circular/square bullets by default
Explanation: <ul> default: disc bullets. <ol> default: decimal numbers. Both customisable with CSS.

QuestionText: The <table> attribute 'border' adds a visible border around cells
Explanation: <table border='1'> adds a 1-pixel border. Modern practice: use CSS border property instead.

QuestionText: Inline CSS uses the 'style' attribute directly on an HTML element
Options: D) Inline CSS is in a file
Explanation:
Inline:

Text

. Highest specificity but hardest to maintain.

QuestionText: The href attribute in <link> tag in <head> links an external CSS file
Explanation: <link rel='stylesheet' href='styles.css'> in <head> attaches an external CSS file.

QuestionText: External CSS file has .css extension
Explanation: External stylesheets are saved with .css extension (e.g. styles.css, main.css).

QuestionText: HTML5 introduced the <video> and <audio> tags for embedding media
Options: C) Flash player is used instead
Explanation: HTML5 <video> and <audio> elements allow embedding media directly without plugins like Flash.

QuestionText: The <meta charset='UTF-8'> tag specifies the character encoding of the page
Explanation: UTF-8 encoding supports all Unicode characters; <meta charset='UTF-8'> ensures correct text rendering.

QuestionText: A favicon is the small icon shown in the browser tab for a website
Options: C) Favicon is a CSS property
D) Favicon is a JavaScript file
Explanation: Favicon: the small icon (16x16 or 32x32 px) linked in <head> that represents a website in browser tabs and bookmarks.

QuestionText: The <strong> tag has the same visual effect as <b> but also carries semantic meaning
Options: C) They are identical in all ways
Explanation: Both render bold, but <strong> indicates the text is of strong importance to browsers and screen readers.

QuestionText: A URL has components: protocol, domain, path, and optional query string
Options: D) URL has only the page name
Explanation: URL structure: https://www.example.com/page?key=value (protocol://domain/path?query)

QuestionText: HTML comments are written as <!-- comment --> and are not displayed
Explanation: HTML comments: <!-- This is a comment --> are invisible in the browser but visible in source code.

QuestionText: The W3C sets standards for HTML and web technologies
Explanation: W3C (World Wide Web Consortium), founded by Tim Berners-Lee, develops and maintains web standards (HTML, CSS, etc.).

QuestionText: HTTP port 80 and HTTPS port 443 are the standard default ports
Explanation: Default ports: HTTP = 80, HTTPS = 443. These are standard well-known port numbers for web traffic.
